content_html:
Eggs can be frozen when removed from their shells and prepared correctly, but whole eggs should not be frozen in the shell because the contents expand and can crack it. Whites, yolks, or beaten whole eggs freeze best in clean containers and useful portions.

Do not freeze whole eggs in the shell

The liquid expands as it freezes and can crack the shell, allowing contamination and producing an uneven texture. Crack eggs into a clean container before freezing.

Beat whole eggs before portioning

Gently combine yolk and white without whipping in excess air and divide into amounts that match common recipes. Label the container with the equivalent number of eggs and the date.

Yolks need special preparation to preserve texture

Yolks alone can thicken or gel when frozen. Follow a reliable method that uses a small amount of salt or sugar depending on the final use, and label clearly whether the batch is intended for sweet or savory recipes.

Thaw in the refrigerator and cook as appropriate

Move the portion to the refrigerator and use it once thawed. Follow the same hygiene practices as with fresh eggs and do not freeze eggs that have already spent too long at room temperature.
